ei.title: Volunteering at an Animal Sanctuary by Mia Watson
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: As the leader of our school club Care for Animals, I organized a volunteer trip to an animal sanctuary for my club members. An animal sanctuary is a special place where rescued, injured, or abused animals can live in a safe and caring environment. All the club members and I agreed that the sanctuary would be the perfect place to learn about animal care. Excited for a new experience, we set out to volunteer. July 29, Monday Our club arrived at the Free Animals sanctuary. Jane, the staff member in charge of animal care, welcomed us with a big smile and gave us a tour of the facility. It was amazing to see bears and elephants moving freely in a large field. Our tasks for the day included cleaning the shelter and preparing food for the animals. While cleaning the habitats, we checked if there were any hazards that could harm the animals. Then, we helped prepare the food by cutting up fruits and vegetables and dividing them into several large baskets. For old elephants with weak teeth, we chopped bananas instead of the sugarcane that they usually eat. Spending the whole day helping out with the animals was an incredible experience for me. It was a rewarding experience, and I was impressed with the attention the staff members gave to all the animals. July 30, Tuesday Today, we did something special for Ben and Lily. These two baby bears were rescued after they had been raised illegally in a tiny cage on a farm for many years. To help the bears restore their natural instincts, we carried out some special activities known as “behavioral enrichment.” For example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears. First, we made several holes in a log and filled them with honey. Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on trees near the bears’ habitat. As bears are intelligent and curious creatures, they can become bored and stressed when lacking mental and physical stimulation. The honey-log feeders stimulate their natural curiosity and keep them as active as they would be in the wild. After a while, Ben and Lily approached the feeders and started eating the honey inside. They are so cute! July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly elephant. After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain. In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which involves using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors. When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it. We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit. This training helps reduce the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination. The good news is Molly seems to be adapting well, and I expect her to get better soon. August 1, Thursday On the last day, we were called to the rescue center due to a sudden emergency. Some dehydrated birds had fallen out of the sky in the city and were brought to the center. Following the veterinarian’s guidance, we provided water to the birds while the vets treated their broken wings and legs and injected them with vitamins for a speedy recovery. It was shocking that this type of accident happens every year since the high temperatures dry up water sources in the city. Caring for the birds, I couldn’t help but reflect on the impact of human activities on climate change and how it harms animals. Saying goodbye to the animals and staff, I felt grateful for the opportunity to volunteer. From this experience, I learned the importance of treating animals with respect and care. I also came to realize that humans are just another kind of animal and share the Earth with all other living creatures. To improve animal welfare, I’ll work hard with Care for Animals members. Hopefully, I’ll have the chance to volunteer at another sanctuary next summer. Deep Learning Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight species, all living in very different habitats around the world. Polar bears, for example, live in the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America. These bears should have the freedom to live, but they are often killed when they come into contact with humans. One of the worst examples of this is bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to the constant demand. Governments and animal welfare organizations make persistent attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals are born with the right to be respected, progress has been made in animal rights. However, some animals are still not fully protected outside the law, and need more of our attention and care.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: moved→moving. 지각동사 see+목적어+현재분사(능동)
det.analysis:
① welcomed ✅ — Jane이 우리를 맞이했다는 과거시제로 맞아요.
② moved ❌ — 'see + 목적어 + -ing(현재분사)'는 '~가 …하고 있는 것을 보다'예요. 코끼리가 스스로 자유롭게 움직이는 능동이라 moving이 맞아요. moved(과거분사)를 쓰면 '움직여지는' 수동이 되어 어색해요 ←정답
③ dividing ✅ — 'by cutting ~ and dividing ~'에서 앞의 cutting과 짝을 이루는 동명사라 맞아요.
④ chopped ✅ — 바나나를 잘게 잘랐다는 과거시제로 맞아요.
det.tip: see + 목적어 + 현재분사(-ing) = 능동 / see + 목적어 + 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: stimulates→stimulate. 주어 The honey-log feeders(복수)
det.analysis:
① raised ✅ — 'had been raised'는 과거완료 수동태(길러졌었다)로 맞아요.
② hung ✅ — hang(걸다)의 과거형이 hung이라 맞아요.
③ lacking ✅ — 'when lacking ~'은 '~가 부족할 때'라는 분사구문(when they lack)이라 맞아요.
④ stimulates ❌ — 주어가 The honey-log feeders(먹이통들, 복수)라서 동사도 복수형 stimulate여야 해요. 단수형 stimulates는 틀려요 ←정답
det.tip: 주어가 복수(feeders)면 동사는 s를 뺀 stimulate. 주어-동사 수일치

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: hunting→hunted. are + 과거분사 수동태(사냥당하다)
det.analysis:
① fascinating ✅ — '흥미를 끄는'이라는 뜻의 형용사(감정을 일으키는 쪽은 -ing)로 맞아요.
② killed ✅ — 'are killed'는 '죽임을 당한다'는 수동태라 맞아요.
③ hunting ❌ — 곰이 사람에게 사냥을 '당하는' 것이라 'are hunted'(수동태, 과거분사)여야 해요. are hunting은 '곰이 사냥한다'는 능동/진행이 되어 틀려요 ←정답
④ allowing ✅ — 콤마 뒤에서 '그리고 ~하면서'로 이어주는 분사구문이라 allowing이 맞아요.
det.tip: be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.) = 수동태. bears are hunted = 곰이 사냥당하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: strong→weak. 이빨이 약한 늙은 코끼리라 바나나를 잘게 잘라줌
det.analysis:
① hazards(위험 요소) ✅ — 동물을 해칠 수 있는 위험 요소를 확인했다는 문맥에 맞아요.
② strong(튼튼한) ❌ — 이빨이 튼튼하면 사탕수수를 그대로 먹을 수 있으니 바나나를 잘게 잘라줄 이유가 없어요. 원문은 weak(약한)이 맞아요 ←정답
③ rewarding(보람 있는) ✅ — 하루 종일 동물을 도운 경험이 보람 있었다는 문맥에 맞아요.
④ tiny(아주 작은) ✅ — 좁은 우리에서 불법으로 길러졌다는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: weak teeth(약한 이빨) → 그래서 바나나를 잘게 잘라줌. strong이면 앞뒤가 안 맞음

questions.passage: July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an ①<u>elderly</u> elephant.  After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a ②<u>twisted</u> spine and foot pain. When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit.  This training helps ③<u>increase</u> the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination.  The good news is Molly seems to be adapting well, and I expect her to get better soon.  August 1, Thursday On the last day, we were called to the rescue center due to a sudden emergency.  Some dehydrated birds had fallen out of the sky in the city and were brought to the center.  Following the veterinarian’s guidance, we provided water to the birds while the vets treated their broken wings and legs and injected them with vitamins for a speedy recovery.  It was shocking that this type of accident happens every year since the high temperatures dry up water ④<u>sources</u> in the city.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: increase→reduce. 훈련은 동물의 스트레스를 줄여줌
det.analysis:
① elderly(나이 든) ✅ — Molly가 나이 든 코끼리라는 문맥에 맞아요.
② twisted(뒤틀린) ✅ — 오래 관광객을 태워 척추가 뒤틀렸다는 문맥에 맞아요.
③ increase(늘리다) ❌ — 긍정 강화 훈련은 치료 같은 상황에서 동물이 겪는 스트레스를 '줄여' 주는 것이라 reduce(줄이다)가 맞아요. increase(늘리다)면 정반대가 돼요 ←정답
④ sources(원천) ✅ — 높은 기온이 도시의 물 공급원을 마르게 한다는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: This training helps reduce the stress = 훈련이 스트레스를 줄인다. increase면 반대

questions.passage: July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly elephant.  After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain.  In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in __________, which involves using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors.  When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit.  This training helps reduce the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: positive reinforcement training = 긍정 강화 훈련(보상으로 바람직한 행동 유도)
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤에 'which involves using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors(보상을 사용해 바람직한 행동을 유도하는)'라는 설명이 나와요. 보상을 준다는 것이 핵심 단서예요.
✅ ① positive reinforcement training(긍정 강화 훈련) — 보상으로 좋은 행동을 유도하는 훈련이라 딱 맞아요 ←정답
❌ ② strict punishment training(엄격한 처벌 훈련) — 보상이 아니라 처벌이라 반대예요.
❌ ③ intensive physical training(고강도 체력 훈련) — 체력 훈련은 보상과 무관해요.
❌ ④ basic obedience training(기본 복종 훈련) — 보상으로 유도한다는 내용과 초점이 달라요.
det.tip: rewards(보상) → positive reinforcement(긍정 강화). 처벌이 아니라 보상이 핵심

questions.passage: One of the worst examples of this is bear bile farming.  Brown bears in Eurasia and North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price for traditional Asian medicine.  Although bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to __________.  Governments and animal welfare organizations make persistent attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe places.  Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals are born with the right to be respected, progress has been made in animal rights.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: the constant demand = 끊임없는 수요(그래서 금지에도 계속됨)
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 '많은 나라에서 금지되어 있지만 계속된다(is prohibited ~ but it continues)'라고 나와요. 금지에도 없어지지 않는 이유는 사려는 사람이 계속 있기 때문이에요.
❌ ① the high price(높은 가격) — 담즙이 비싸게 팔리긴 하지만, 계속되는 직접적인 이유는 가격이 아니라 수요예요.
✅ ② the constant demand(끊임없는 수요) — 사려는 수요가 계속 있어서 담즙 농장이 사라지지 않는다는 흐름에 맞아요 ←정답
❌ ③ the traditional medicine(전통 의학) — 담즙이 전통 의학용으로 팔리지만, '수요' 때문에 계속된다는 표현이 더 정확해요.
❌ ④ the persistent attempts(끈질긴 시도) — 이 시도는 농장을 '찾아 없애려는' 노력이라, 오히려 농장을 막는 쪽이에요.
det.tip: prohibited but continues due to ~ = 금지에도 계속되는 이유 = 끊임없는 수요(demand)

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 보호구역 = 구조·부상·학대당한 동물이 안전하게 사는 곳
det.analysis:
❌ ① — 글쓴이는 동아리 회원들과 '함께' 봉사를 떠났어요(organized a volunteer trip for my club members).
❌ ② — 이빨이 약한 늙은 코끼리에게는 사탕수수 대신 바나나를 잘게 잘라 주었어요(chopped bananas instead of the sugarcane).
❌ ③ — Jane은 봉사자들에게 시설을 견학시켜 주었어요(gave us a tour of the facility).
✅ ④ — 보호구역은 구조되거나 다치거나 학대당한 동물이 안전한 환경에서 살 수 있는 곳이라고 했어요 ←정답
det.tip: 본문 첫 부분: a special place where rescued, injured, or abused animals can live in a safe ~ environment

ch: 글쓴이는 동아리 회원들과 떨어져 혼자서 봉사 활동을 떠났다.
봉사자들은 이빨이 약한 코끼리에게도 사탕수수를 그대로 주었다.
Jane은 너무 바빠서 봉사자들에게 시설을 안내하지 못했다.
동물 보호구역은 위기에 처했던 동물들이 안전하게 지낼 수 있는 공간이다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 먹이통은 서식지 근처 나무에 걸었고, 호기심을 자극해 곰이 꿀을 먹게 함
det.analysis:
① ✅ — Ben과 Lily는 여러 해 동안 좁은 우리에서 불법으로 길러졌어요(raised illegally in a tiny cage for many years).
❌ ② — 먹이통을 멀리 둔 게 아니라 서식지 '근처' 나무에 걸었고(hung ~ on trees near the bears' habitat), 곰의 호기심을 자극해 꿀을 먹게 하려는 목적이었어요 ←정답(일치하지 않음)
③ ✅ — 곰은 지적이고 호기심 많은 동물이라고 했어요(intelligent and curious creatures).
④ ✅ — 먹이통이 곰의 자연스러운 호기심을 자극한다고 했어요(stimulate their natural curiosity).
det.tip: near the bears' habitat = 서식지 '근처'. 멀리 둔 게 아님

ch: Ben과 Lily는 오랫동안 좁은 우리에서 불법으로 길러졌다.
봉사자들은 곰이 꿀을 찾지 못하도록 먹이통을 서식지에서 멀리 두었다.
꿀 통나무 먹이통은 곰의 자연스러운 호기심을 자극한다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: Molly에게 가장 좋아하는 과일 수박을 보상으로 줌
det.analysis:
❌ ① — Molly는 25년 동안 관광객을 태워 척추가 뒤틀린 거예요(After spending 25 years). 5년이 아니에요.

Deep Learning Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight species, all living in very different habitats around the world.  Polar bears, for example, live in the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America.  These bears should have the freedom to live, but they are often killed when they come into contact with humans.  One of the worst examples of this is bear bile farming.  Brown bears in Eurasia and North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price for traditional Asian medicine.  Although bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to the constant demand.  Governments and animal welfare organizations make persistent attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe places.  Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals are born with the right to be respected, progress has been made in animal rights.

questions.passage: To help the bears restore their natural instincts, we carried out some special activities known as “behavioral enrichment. ” For example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears. det.korean: 우리는 통나무에 여러 개의 구멍을 만들었다
det.analysis:
'우리는 ~ 만들었다'가 핵심이라 주어 we + 과거동사 made로 시작해요.
→ 무엇을 만들었나요? '여러 개의 구멍'이니 several holes.
→ 어디에? '통나무에'는 전치사 in + a log.
→ 순서: we(주어) + made(동사) + several holes(목적어) + in a log(장소) = we made several holes in a log (7단어)
det.tip: 주어(we) + 동사(made) + 목적어(several holes) + 장소(in a log) 순서

In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which ①<u>involving</u> using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors.  When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: involving → involves. 계속적 용법 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 동사가 필요
det.analysis:
밑줄 부분은 'positive reinforcement training, which ① involving using rewards ~'예요.
→ 콤마 뒤 which는 앞의 training(훈련)을 받는 계속적 용법 관계대명사예요. 이때 which는 문장의 주어 역할을 하므로 뒤에는 반드시 '동사'가 와야 해요.
→ involving은 -ing 형태(준동사)라서 동사 자리에 올 수 없어요. 선행사 training이 3인칭 단수이므로 동사도 3인칭 단수형 involves로 고쳐야 해요.
→ 정답: involves
det.tip: 콤마 + which(주격 관계대명사) 뒤에는 동사 필요. involving(준동사) → involves(동사)

det.korean: 탈수된 새들이 하늘에서 떨어졌었다

→ 어떤 새? '탈수된 새들'이니 dehydrated birds(형용사 + 명사).

det.tip: 과거완료 = had + 과거분사(fallen). fall-fell-fallen. out of the sky = 하늘에서
